reading.body:
J-Curve Technologies cannot be counted as an Arizona data center, because no operator, registration, or coverage confirms it exists at the Tempe address.

The entry rests on a single OpenStreetMap node at coordinates that reverse geocode to 2005 West 14th Street, Tempe, with no business name attached. No operator website, business registration, or press coverage was found, and the research status is exhausted. The name itself is a finance term for a growth pattern, not an established presence in the data center industry. Nothing here shows server rooms, colocation space, or equipment.

This matters for AI because grid load is counted facility by facility, and a row like this one contributes nothing countable. Arizona has 56 mapped data center facilities, and only 4 publish power specifications, totaling 512 MW. This site publishes no megawatts, so it cannot be ranked among them or added to any estimate of state load.

What the data does not tell you is whether a real facility operates here under a different name, or whether the tag was simply wrong. It also does not connect this location to any other facility in the batch, which sits more than 20 miles away. The honest reading is a gap in the map, not a data center.
